results.title: Resolvent of two clauses
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and $C$, $D$ clauses. The resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$ is the clause consisting of the literals of $C$ other than $(x, \mathrm{true})$, in order, followed by the literals of $D$ other than $(x, \mathrm{false})$, in order.

results.title: Resolution rule soundness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and $C$, $D$ clauses. Every assignment that satisfies both $C$ and $D$ satisfies the resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$.

results.title: Resolution derivability
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Given a CNF formula $\varphi$, the clauses derivable from $\varphi$ by resolution form the smallest set $S$ of clauses that contains every clause of $\varphi$ and, for every variable $x$ and all clauses $C, D \in S$ such that $C$ contains the literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ and $D$ contains the literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$, contains the resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$.

results.title: Soundness of resolution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula. Every clause derivable by resolution from $\varphi$ is satisfied by every assignment that satisfies $\varphi$.

results.title: Refutable formulas are unsatisfiable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the empty clause is derivable by resolution from a CNF formula $\varphi$, then $\varphi$ is not satisfiable.

results.title: Clauses of a restricted formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and $\ell$ a literal. A clause $C$ belongs to the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ if and only if there is a clause $C_0$ of $\varphi$ that does not contain $\ell$ such that $C$ is the restriction of $C_0$ by $\ell$.

results.title: Lifting lemma
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula, $x$ a variable and $b$ a Boolean value. If a clause $D$ is derivable by resolution from the restriction of $\varphi$ by the literal $(x, b)$, then some clause $D_0$ is derivable by resolution from $\varphi$ such that every literal of $D_0$ is either a literal of $D$ or the complementary literal $(x, \lnot b)$.

results.title: Unsatisfiable formulas without variables contain the empty clause
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a CNF formula $\varphi$ has no variables and is not satisfiable, then the empty clause is one of the clauses of $\varphi$.

results.title: Refutation completeness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Refutation completeness of resolution: every unsatisfiable CNF formula has a resolution derivation of the empty clause.

results.title: Soundness and refutation completeness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A CNF formula has a resolution refutation iff it is unsatisfiable.

results.title: Rational groups, conjugacy form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is rational if every element $g \in G$ is conjugate to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$, where an element of infinite order has order $0$, so that only $k = 1$ is coprime to it. For finite groups this is the classical equivalent form of the condition that all ordinary characters of $G$ are rational-valued.

results.title: Sylow 2-subgroups of rational groups need not be rational (Kourovka 16.36)

results.title: Kourovka 21.137, main question
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that there is a prime $p$ such that for every finite $p$-group $G$ and every subgroup $P$ of $G$ whose underlying set is exactly the set $\{x^p : x \in G\}$ of $p$-th powers in $G$, the subgroup $P$ is powerful: its commutator subgroup $[P, P]$ is contained in the subgroup $P^m$ generated by the $m$-th powers of the elements of $P$, where $m = p$ for odd $p$ and $m = 4$ for $p = 2$.

results.title: Kourovka 21.137, odd-prime form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that there is an odd prime $p$ such that for every finite $p$-group $G$ of exponent $p^2$ and every subgroup $P$ of $G$ whose underlying set is exactly the set $\{x^p : x \in G\}$ of $p$-th powers in $G$, the subgroup $P$ is abelian.

results.title: Kourovka 21.137 fails for every prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every prime $p$ there is a finite $p$-group $G$ with a subgroup $P$ whose underlying set is exactly the set $\{x^p : x \in G\}$ of $p$-th powers in $G$, such that $P$ is not powerful: the commutator subgroup $[P, P]$ is not contained in the subgroup $P^m$ generated by the $m$-th powers of the elements of $P$, where $m = p$ for odd $p$ and $m = 4$ for $p = 2$.

results.title: Kourovka 21.137 fails for every odd prime

results.title: Kourovka Problem 16.59 (finite groups as outer automorphism groups)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every finite group $K$ there are a finite group $G$ and a surjective homomorphism $\mathrm{Aut}(G) \to K$ whose kernel is the group $\mathrm{Inn}(G)$ of inner automorphisms of $G$, that is, $K$ is isomorphic to $\mathrm{Out}(G) = \mathrm{Aut}(G) / \mathrm{Inn}(G)$.

results.title: Every finite group is the outer automorphism group of a finite group
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite group $K$ there are a finite group $G$ and a surjective homomorphism $\mathrm{Aut}(G) \to K$ whose kernel is the group $\mathrm{Inn}(G)$ of inner automorphisms of $G$; equivalently, $\mathrm{Out}(G) = \mathrm{Aut}(G) / \mathrm{Inn}(G)$ is isomorphic to $K$. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 16.59 is positive.

results.title: Outer automorphism group isomorphic to a given group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For groups $M$ and $G$, the statement that $\operatorname{Out}(M) \cong G$, expressed without forming the quotient: there is a surjective homomorphism $\operatorname{Aut}(M) \to G$ whose kernel is exactly the inner automorphism group $\operatorname{Inn}(M)$, the image of the conjugation map $M \to \operatorname{Aut}(M)$.

results.title: Containment of planar point sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ contains a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ when there are maps $f_X, f_Y : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f_X(x_0) - f_X(x_1) \ge x_0 - x_1$ whenever $x_0 > x_1$ are $x$-coordinates of points of $P$, $f_Y(y_0) - f_Y(y_1) \ge y_0 - y_1$ whenever $y_0 > y_1$ are $y$-coordinates of points of $P$, and $(f_X(x), f_Y(y)) \in S$ for every $(x, y) \in P$.

results.title: Every planar set contains the empty pattern
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ contains the empty set $\emptyset$ in the sense of containment of planar point sets.

results.title: Continuous Turán number in the plane
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $n$ and a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, the continuous Turán number $\operatorname{opx}(n, P)$ is the supremum of the Lebesgue measures $\mu_2(S)$ over all open sets $S \subseteq [0, n]^2$ that do not contain $P$ in the sense of point-set pattern containment; it is $0$ when there is no such set.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the continuous Turán number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $n$ and every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) \ge 0$.

results.title: Continuous Turán number of the empty pattern
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $n$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, \emptyset) = 0$: every set contains the empty pattern, so no set avoids it.

results.title: Rotation and reflection invariance of the continuous Turán number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $n$ and every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, the value $\operatorname{opx}(n, P)$ does not change when $P$ is replaced by its image under the rotation by $90^\circ$, $(x, y) \mapsto (-y, x)$, under the reflection $(x, y) \mapsto (-x, y)$, or under the reflection $(x, y) \mapsto (x, -y)$.

results.title: Translation invariance of the continuous Turán number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a real number, $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ a set and $v \in \mathbb{R}^2$ a vector, and let $P + v = \{p + v : p \in P\}$ be the translate of $P$ by $v$. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P + v) = \operatorname{opx}(n, P)$.

results.title: Monotonicity of the continuous Turán number under containment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a real number and let $P, Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$. If $Q$ contains $P$ in the sense of containment of planar point sets, then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) \le \operatorname{opx}(n, Q)$.

results.title: Monotonicity of the continuous Turán number in the side length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and all real numbers $m \le n$, the continuous Turán numbers satisfy $\operatorname{opx}(m, P) \le \operatorname{opx}(n, P)$.

results.title: Superadditivity of the continuous Turán number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and all real numbers $m, n > 0$, $\operatorname{opx}(m, P) + \operatorname{opx}(n, P) \le \operatorname{opx}(m + n, P)$.

results.title: Increment bound for the continuous Turán number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $n, \delta$ be real numbers with $n > 0$ and $0 < \delta < n$. Then the continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}$ satisfies $\mathrm{opx}(n, P) \le \mathrm{opx}(n + \delta, P)$ and $\mathrm{opx}(n + \delta, P) < \mathrm{opx}(n, P) + 3 n \delta$.

results.title: Continuity of the continuous Turán number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, the continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}(n, P)$ is a continuous function of $n$ on $(0, \infty)$.

results.title: Lower bound on the volume of a staircase region
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a natural number and let $c, n$ be real numbers with $c \ge 0$ and $ct \le n$. Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^t$ be the set of points $y = (y_0, \dots, y_{t-1})$ such that $y_i < n - ic$ for every $i$, $y_{i+1} + c < y_i$ for every $i < t - 1$, and $y_{t-1} > 0$ if $t \ge 1$. Then the $t$-dimensional Lebesgue measure of $X$ is at least $(n/t - c)^t$, where $n/t$ is read as $0$ when $t = 0$.

results.title: Upper bound for stacked horizontal segments
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ be a natural number, let $s, c > 0$ be real numbers, and let $P_{s,t,c} = [0, s] \times \{c, 2c, \dots, tc\}$ be the union of the $t$ horizontal segments of length $s$ at heights $c, 2c, \dots, tc$. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P_{s,t,c}) = O(s^{1/t} n^{2 - 1/t})$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity, with $s$, $t$ and $c$ fixed.

results.title: Linear bound for separated horizontal segments
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $a_i \le b_i$ and $y_i$ be real numbers for $i = 1, \dots, k$, such that the intervals $[a_i, b_i]$ are pairwise disjoint and the heights $y_i$ are pairwise distinct, and let $P = \bigcup_{i=1}^k [a_i, b_i] \times \{y_i\}$. Then the continuous Turán number satisfies $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = O(n)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.

results.title: Containment of a point pattern in a set of grid cells
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set of cells $A \subseteq \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$, each cell written (column, row), contains a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ when there are maps $f_X, f_Y : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $f_X$ is strictly increasing on the set of $x$-coordinates of points of $P$, $f_Y$ is strictly increasing on the set of $y$-coordinates of points of $P$, and $(f_X(x), f_Y(y)) \in A$ for every $(x, y) \in P$.

results.title: The extremal function of the empty pattern vanishes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, $\operatorname{ex}(n, M_\emptyset) = 0$, since every set of cells contains the empty pattern.

results.title: The extremal function of a single point vanishes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every point $p \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the 0-1 matrix extremal function of the one-point pattern $\{p\}$ on the $n \times n$ grid is zero: $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_{\{p\}}) = 0$. Indeed, a single point is contained in every nonempty set of cells.

results.title: Trivial upper bound for the 0-1 matrix extremal function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ a set, and let $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P)$ be the largest number of cells of the $n \times n$ grid $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}^2$ forming a set that does not contain $P$ ($0$ if there is no such set). Then $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P) \le n^2$.

results.title: Inverse Ackermann function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the inverse Ackermann function $\alpha(n)$ is the least natural number $k$ with $n \le A(k, k)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function, given for all natural numbers $m$ and $j$ by $A(0, j) = j + 1$, $A(m + 1, 0) = A(m, 1)$ and $A(m + 1, j + 1) = A(m, A(m + 1, j))$.

results.title: Defining inequality of the inverse Ackermann function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, $n \le A(\alpha(n), \alpha(n))$, where $\alpha$ is the inverse Ackermann function and $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function.

results.title: Upper bound for the inverse Ackermann function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, if $n \le A(k, k)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function, then $\alpha(n) \le k$, where $\alpha$ is the inverse Ackermann function.

results.title: The inverse Ackermann function at 2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inverse Ackermann function $\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha(2) = 1$, since $A(0, 0) = 1 < 2 \le 3 = A(1, 1)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function.

results.title: The inverse Ackermann function at 8
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inverse Ackermann function $\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha(8) = 3$, since $A(2, 2) = 7 < 8 \le 61 = A(3, 3)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function.

results.title: Increment bound for the d-dimensional continuous Turán number

Writing $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q, k)$ for the $k$-dimensional continuous Turán number, we have $n \cdot \mathrm{opx}(n, \Pr(P), d) \le \mathrm{opx}(n, P, d + 1)$.

Then for every real number $n$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d + 1) = n \cdot \mathrm{opx}(n, \mathrm{Pr}(P), d)$.

results.title: Goldstine's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $E^{**}$ be its bidual and let $J : E \to E^{**}$ be the canonical embedding. results.title: Continuous linear functionals on the space of all real functions
results.caption: Theorem
